findings.title: `plural` is defined twice byte-for-byte and inlined three more times
findings.problem: The English-plural suffix rule exists five times in one crate: two byte-identical private `fn plural(n: usize) -> &'static str` definitions (`ledger.rs`, `spill_index.rs`) and three inline `if x == 1 { "" } else { "s" }` expressions (`compact_window::recommend`'s basis sentence, `hook::session_end`'s heartbeat detail, `status`'s hook-row line).
findings.proposal: Add `crates/ss-magic-plugin/src/text.rs` with `pub(crate) fn plural(n: usize) -> &'static str` (the existing body verbatim), declare `mod text;` in `main.rs`, delete both private copies, and replace the three inline expressions with `text::plural(n)`. Every site is in the plugin crate, so the helper does not belong in `ss-magic-core` (no CLI caller exists — grepped).
findings.behavior_preservation: The moved body is unchanged and every call site passes the same `usize` it already tests against 1, so each produces the same `""`/`"s"` and the same rendered line. The inline sites take `usize` fields (`sessions`, `row.files`, `status.hooks.rows`), matching the signature exactly.

findings.title: `ledger::ensure_store` is a byte-identical copy of `heartbeat::ensure_store`, for the same directory
findings.problem: Both functions create the SAME machine-level store directory (`ledger::record` is always handed `heartbeat::store_dir()` / `heartbeat::existing_store_dir()`), at the same mode, with the same `anyhow` context text. `ledger.rs` already imports `crate::heartbeat` (line 74), so the copy buys nothing; if the store's mode or its error wording ever changes, one of the two will be missed.
findings.proposal: Make `heartbeat::ensure_store` `pub(crate)` and delete `ledger::ensure_store`, calling `heartbeat::ensure_store(store)?` from `ledger::record` (ledger.rs:852). `ledger::DIR_MODE` then loses its only use in the module and can go (see F14).
findings.behavior_preservation: The two bodies are textually identical including the `is_dir()` short-circuit, the `recursive(true).mode(DIR_MODE)` builder and the context message; `DIR_MODE` is `0o700` in both modules. Same success value, same error type and text, same side effect.

findings.title: `ledger::transcript_root` re-implements `spill_index::projects_root`, which is public and documents the shared intent
findings.problem: `spill_index::projects_root` is `pub`, has the identical body, and its own doc comment says it is "[d]eliberately the same resolution `plugin::ledger` uses for transcripts ... two different answers to 'where does the harness keep this' would be a bug waiting to happen". The intent is stated but never actually shared, so the two can still drift.
findings.proposal: Delete `ledger::transcript_root` and call `crate::spill_index::projects_root()` at its one use site (`run_backfill`, ledger.rs:1268), keeping the `Only needed by the backfill path` note as a comment there. (If the dependency direction reads badly, hoist the body per F4 instead and have both modules call the hoisted helper.)
findings.behavior_preservation: The bodies are token-for-token the same — same variable names, same empty-string filtering, same `.join("projects")` — so the returned `Option<PathBuf>` is identical for every environment. Neither reads anything else.

findings.title: The `${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}` resolution is hand-written in four modules, two of which already share `non_empty_env`
findings.problem: Four sites answer "where is the harness's config directory" independently. Two are the same expression written twice (`compact_window`, `status`); two more (`ledger`, `spill_index`) re-implement the same rule inline instead of using `status::non_empty_env`, which `compact_window` already reuses for exactly this idiom. The rule is one harness fact and has four owners.
findings.proposal: Add `pub(crate) fn harness_config_dir() -> Option<PathBuf>` beside `status::non_empty_env` (status.rs:878) with the `compact_window`/`status` expression as its body. `compact_window::Sources::from_process` uses `harness_config_dir()?.join("settings.json")`; `status::locate_data_root` uses it directly; `spill_index::projects_root` becomes `Some(harness_config_dir()?.join("projects"))`; `ledger::transcript_root` goes away per F3.
findings.behavior_preservation: `non_empty_env(name)` is `std::env::var(name).ok().filter(|v| !v.is_empty())` — exactly what the two inline copies spell out with `if let Ok(dir) ... if !dir.is_empty()` plus `.ok().filter(...)`, and the fallback joins `.claude` in both spellings. `None` is returned in the same three cases (no `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and no `HOME`, or both empty).

findings.title: Six `usage_error`/`fail` helpers with four different signatures, two of them argument-swapped
findings.problem: Every body is the same three statements — `eprintln!(style::err("error: {message}"))`, `eprintln!(usage)`, exit 2 — but the crate carries four incompatible signatures for it, including `cache::usage_error(message, usage)` and `config::usage_error(usage, message)`, which take the SAME two `&str` in opposite order. A reader (or a future edit) moving between verbs has to re-derive the argument order and the return type each time, and swapping them silently prints the usage banner as the error line.
findings.proposal: Put `pub(crate) fn usage_error(message: &str, usage: &str) -> ExitCode` and `pub(crate) fn fail(message: &str) -> ExitCode` in the new `text.rs` from F1 (or beside `atomic`), each with the existing body and `ExitCode::from(2)`. Every verb passes its own `USAGE`/`COST_USAGE` const; the two `Result<ExitCode>` call sites become `return Ok(usage_error(msg, COST_USAGE))`; `checklist::refused()` stays as the local name for the code but the printing helpers go.
findings.behavior_preservation: All six write the same two lines to stderr in the same order through `style::err` and return exit code 2 (`checklist::refused()` is `ExitCode::from(2)`); only the wrapper `Ok(...)` moves from the callee to the caller, which is not observable. `compact_window::fail` takes `String` and `checklist::fail` takes `String`; both call sites already build the string with `format!`, so `&str` at the boundary prints identically.

findings.title: Two operator messages re-spell `WINDOW_KEY` and `SETTINGS_LOCAL_REL` as literals in the file that owns them
findings.evidence:
compact_window.rs:659      "Tip: no autoCompactWindow is configured for this repository. \
compact_window.rs:660       `ss-magic-plugin compact-window --recommend` sizes one from its recorded \
compact_window.rs:829          "Nothing was written. `--set` is the only write this verb makes, and only to \
compact_window.rs:830           .claude/settings.local.json."
findings.problem: `WINDOW_KEY` (line 118) and `SETTINGS_LOCAL_REL` (line 89) are defined in this same file and interpolated everywhere else that names them (`run_core` at 250/264/266, `render_text`'s section header at 783), but these two messages hand-type the values. `enable_tip` additionally wraps a placeholder-free string in `format!`, which is what hides that it could have interpolated.
findings.proposal: In `enable_tip`, change the literal to `format!("Tip: no {WINDOW_KEY} is configured for this repository. ...")`. In `render_text`, wrap the closing line in `format!` so it ends `... and only to {SETTINGS_LOCAL_REL}."`. Consider making `WINDOW_KEY` `pub(crate)` so `status.rs:1051` and `hook/session_start.rs:219`, which also hand-type `autoCompactWindow`, can stop doing so (separate partitions).
findings.behavior_preservation: `WINDOW_KEY` is exactly `"autoCompactWindow"` and `SETTINGS_LOCAL_REL` exactly `".claude/settings.local.json"`, so both interpolations render byte-identical strings; `style::info` receives the same text. `format!` versus a `&'static str` is invisible to `style::info`, which takes `impl Display`/`AsRef<str>` at both existing call sites.

findings.title: The `USAGE` banner hand-types the window bounds and both settings paths that are consts three lines above it
findings.problem: The runtime error `parse_args` produces interpolates `{WINDOW_MIN}-{WINDOW_MAX}`, but the usage banner a person actually reads next to it hand-types `100000-1000000` (and `.claude/settings.local.json`, `.claude/settings.json`, `autoCompactWindow`). A `const &str` cannot interpolate, so changing a bound would leave the banner contradicting the refusal it is printed beside.
findings.proposal: Replace the const with `fn usage() -> String` containing the same text as a `format!` with `{WINDOW_MIN}`, `{WINDOW_MAX}`, `{SETTINGS_LOCAL_REL}`, `{SETTINGS_PROJECT_REL}` and `{WINDOW_KEY}` placeholders, and update its two call sites (`run`'s Help arm at line 168 and `usage_error` at line 839) to `println!("{}", usage())` / `eprintln!("{}", usage())`. No test references `USAGE` (grepped), so nothing else moves.
findings.behavior_preservation: The interpolated values are exactly the literals in the banner today (`100_000` prints as `100000`, `1_000_000` as `1000000`, and the two path consts and the key const are the same strings), so both call sites emit byte-identical output on the same stream.

findings.title: A bare `64 * 1024` line buffer sits beside the named `READ_BUF_BYTES` in the same scan pipeline
findings.problem: The module names every other tuning number (`HEAD_SCAN_BYTES`, `READ_BUF_BYTES`, `PRUNE_TRIGGER_BYTES`'s peers in `heartbeat`), but the per-line `Vec` capacity — the second-largest allocation in the hot scan — is an unexplained literal four times smaller than the reader capacity two functions above it.
findings.proposal: Add `const LINE_BUF_BYTES: usize = 64 * 1024;` immediately after `READ_BUF_BYTES` with a one-line doc saying it is the starting capacity for one transcript line (it grows for a larger one), and use it at line 683.
findings.behavior_preservation: A named const with the same value produces the same `Vec::with_capacity` argument; capacity is not observable in output and the vector still grows on demand for longer lines.

findings.title: `rows_for_repository` resolves every root in the whole ledger before truncating to 20 rows
findings.problem: `belongs` runs `root_belongs_to` — an `is_dir()` plus `git::discover::roots`, a filesystem walk that falls back to two `git` subprocesses when the walk declines — once per DISTINCT root in the entire ledger, including every root belonging to other repositories and every ancient row that the `truncate(limit)` (20, from `compact_window::RECOMMEND_ROWS`) throws away. On a machine with a long history across many repositories that is a walk (or a `git` spawn) per foreign worktree on every `--recommend` and every `status`.
findings.proposal: Reorder to cheap-filter, sort, then resolve lazily: collect the `peak_context_tokens.is_some()` rows, `sort_by` the same comparator, then `into_iter().filter(|row| row.root.iter().chain(row.also_roots.iter()).any(&mut belongs)).take(limit).collect()`. The memoizing `resolved` map stays as is.
findings.behavior_preservation: The comparator is a total order over the rows (ts, then session id, which is the ledger's unique key), so filtering a sorted sequence and taking the first `limit` yields the same rows in the same order as sorting a filtered sequence and truncating. Only the number of `git::discover::roots` calls drops; the returned `Vec<Row>` is identical, and no other side effect exists (discovery is read-only).

findings.title: `--recommend` reads and parses each project settings file twice per run
findings.problem: `detect_override` reads and JSON-parses `.claude/settings.json` and `.claude/settings.local.json` through `env_value_in` -> `read_settings_object`, and `recommend_report` then reads and parses the same two files again through `read_window`. Four reads where two would do, and the two halves of the report can disagree if the file changes between them.
findings.proposal: Inside `recommend_report`, parse each of the two project files once (a small `HashMap<PathBuf, ExistingSettings>` or two locals) and pass the parsed `ExistingSettings` to both consumers: split `read_window` into the current path-taking wrapper plus `window_from(rel, &ExistingSettings) -> WindowSetting`, and give `detect_override` an equivalent `env_value_from(&ExistingSettings)`. `window_configured`, `enable_tip` and `status` keep the path-taking wrappers unchanged.
findings.behavior_preservation: `read_settings_object` is pure with respect to the file's bytes, so one read feeding both consumers yields the same `WindowSetting` and the same `OverrideLocation` list, including the note text for a malformed or non-object file. Impact is modest (a human verb over two small files); the consistency gain is the real point.

findings.title: `read_settings_object` pre-checks existence instead of handling `NotFound`, unlike `ledger::read` next door
findings.problem: Check-then-act: an extra `stat` per call (four per `--recommend`, see F10) and the classic TOCTOU shape — a file removed between `exists()` and the read surfaces as a hard `Err` rather than `Absent`. `ledger::read`, in this same partition, already does it the other way and is the pattern to copy.
findings.proposal: Drop the `exists()` branch and match on the read: `match fs::read_to_string(path) { Err(e) if e.kind() == ErrorKind::NotFound => return Ok(ExistingSettings::Absent), Err(e) => return Err(e).with_context(...), Ok(raw) => raw }`, then parse as today.
findings.behavior_preservation: For every non-racing input the answer is unchanged: an absent file yields `Absent` either way, and a present file takes the same read-and-parse path with the same context message (a directory or a permission error still reports `reading <path>`). The only difference is the racing removal, which becomes `Absent` instead of an I/O error — the same answer the pre-check would have given a moment earlier.

findings.title: The same `BTreeSet<String>` to comma-list chain is written twice in `report`, cloning every element
findings.evidence:
ledger.rs:1462          group.branches
ledger.rs:1464              .iter()
ledger.rs:1465              .cloned()
ledger.rs:1466              .collect::<Vec<_>>()
ledger.rs:1467              .join(", ")
ledger.rs:1494          group.unpriced.iter().cloned().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ")
findings.problem: Two identical five-link chains thirty lines apart render a `BTreeSet<String>` as a comma-separated list, each allocating a clone of every string only to drop it after the join.
findings.proposal: Add `fn comma_list(items: &BTreeSet<String>) -> String { items.iter().map(String::as_str).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ") }` beside `plural`/`compact` at the end of `ledger.rs`, and call it from both sites (the `branches` site keeps its `if group.branches.is_empty() { "-" }` arm).
findings.behavior_preservation: `BTreeSet` iteration order is unchanged, so the joined string is byte-identical; `join` over `Vec<&str>` produces the same bytes as over `Vec<String>`, and the clones were never observed.

findings.title: Two `.json` writers pass a `.jsonl` temp suffix copied from the ledger writer
findings.evidence:
ledger.rs:355      &store.join(OFFSETS_FILE_NAME),          // "transcript-offsets.json"
ledger.rs:357      ".offsets-",
ledger.rs:358      ".jsonl",
ledger.rs:1146     let path = dir.join(format!("{PRICE_TABLE_VERSION}.json"));
ledger.rs:1154     atomic::write_atomically(&path, &body, ".prices-", ".jsonl", None, Some(FILE_MODE), false)
findings.problem: `write_offsets` writes `transcript-offsets.json` and `snapshot_prices` writes `prices/<version>.json`, but both stage through a temp file suffixed `.jsonl` — the suffix `replace_row` correctly uses for `cost.jsonl`, copied to two files that are plain JSON. Anyone debugging a leftover temp file (or writing a cleanup glob) is told the wrong format.
findings.proposal: Pass `".json"` as the suffix at ledger.rs:358 and ledger.rs:1154; leave `replace_row`'s `".jsonl"` (ledger.rs:1127) alone.
findings.behavior_preservation: The suffix only names the `tempfile::Builder` staging file, which is renamed onto the target before the call returns; the final path, bytes and mode are unchanged, and no test asserts on a temp name (grepped for `.offsets-` / `.prices-`).

findings.title: `DIR_MODE`/`FILE_MODE` are redeclared in ten modules, and `FILE_MODE` names two different values
findings.problem: `DIR_MODE = 0o700` appears in 8 modules and `FILE_MODE = 0o600` in 8 (bypass, cache, expect_artifact, heartbeat, ledger, scratchpad, tmproot, hook/{file_changed,pre_compact,subagent_stop}) — every copy expressing the one "machine-local state is owner-only" rule. Worse, `setup_ci::FILE_MODE` is `0o644`, so the SAME name means two different modes depending on the file you are reading, while the same 0o644 is called `NEW_FILE_MODE` in `compact_window` and `checklist::verbs`.
findings.proposal: Declare the three modes once beside the shared writer they are all passed to — `atomic.rs` — as `pub(crate) const OWNER_DIR_MODE: u32 = 0o700; pub(crate) const OWNER_FILE_MODE: u32 = 0o600; pub(crate) const COMMITTED_FILE_MODE: u32 = 0o644;`, and have every module import them instead of redeclaring. `setup_ci`'s `FILE_MODE` becomes `COMMITTED_FILE_MODE`, removing the name collision.
findings.behavior_preservation: Every replacement is the same octal value the module already used, passed to the same `DirBuilder::mode` / `atomic::write_atomically` argument, so every created file and directory keeps its current permissions. This is a rename, not a change of policy — the owner-only modes stay owner-only.

findings.title: Nine `pub` items in these two verbs have no consumer outside their own module
findings.problem: A grep for each symbol outside its own file finds nothing in production code: `OFFSETS_FILE_NAME`, `PRICES_DIR_NAME`, `PRICE_TABLE_VERSION`, `ledger_path`, `transcript_tree`, `RECOMMEND_ROWS` and `RECOMMEND_SCHEMA_VERSION` are used only inside their module (and the sibling `tests.rs`, which reaches private items anyway). `LEDGER_FILE_NAME` and `read` have exactly one outside consumer each, and both are test modules (`compact_window/tests.rs`, `hook/session_end/tests.rs`), so `pub(crate)` is the widest they need. The `pub` surface reads as a promise of an external contract this binary crate cannot have.
findings.proposal: Make `OFFSETS_FILE_NAME`, `PRICES_DIR_NAME`, `PRICE_TABLE_VERSION`, `ledger_path`, `transcript_tree`, `RECOMMEND_ROWS` and `RECOMMEND_SCHEMA_VERSION` private (`const`/`fn` with no visibility modifier), and narrow `LEDGER_FILE_NAME` and `read` to `pub(crate)`. Leave `record`, `rows_for_repository`, `Ingest`, `Recorded`, `Row`, `Tokens`, `Basis`, `run`, `recommend_report`, `Sources` and `OVERRIDE_ENV` as they are — those have real cross-module callers.
findings.behavior_preservation: This is a binary crate with no downstream consumers, so no item is reachable from outside; a sibling `tests.rs` sees its parent module's private items regardless. Nothing about the compiled behavior changes — `cargo build --workspace` and `cargo test --workspace` are the check.

findings.title: The crate's timestamp helpers live in `scratchpad` and are imported by a dozen unrelated modules
findings.problem: `format_rfc3339` and `now_secs` are general clock helpers, but they are owned by `scratchpad`, whose subject is the `.superset/.magic/` state tree. Twelve modules — the ledger, the heartbeat, the release check, the spill index, the checklist, four hook handlers, status, cache, bypass, expect_artifact — reach into that module for a time format they have nothing else to do with, which makes `scratchpad` look like a dependency of half the crate.
findings.proposal: Move `format_rfc3339` and `now_secs` verbatim into the `text.rs` proposed in F1 (or a dedicated `clock.rs`), re-export them from `scratchpad` for one change if a big-bang import rewrite is unwanted, and update the `use` lines. No body changes.
findings.behavior_preservation: A pure move of two functions with no state; every caller gets the same formatting and the same `SystemTime`-derived seconds. The risk is purely mechanical (import churn), which the compiler catches.

nothing_to_flag: Rubric 1 item 2 (standard-library or runtime primitives): the candidates here are not behavior-equivalent. `ledger::contains` (ledger.rs:807) has no stable std byte-slice substring search, and it deliberately runs on the raw 256-byte head BEFORE the UTF-8 check, so `str::contains` cannot replace it. `group_rows`'s `partial_cmp(...).unwrap_or(Equal)` (ledger.rs:1393-1395) is NOT `f64::total_cmp` — they order NaN differently. `hashing`'s hand-rolled SHA-256 and FNV-1a are pinned by structure-pins.

Rubric 1 item 3 (platform / framework / downstream guarantees): nothing in these two verbs hand-maintains a guarantee the platform already owns. The atomic-write, fd-lock and gitignore guarantees are already delegated to `atomic::write_atomically`, `tmproot::with_lock` and `gitignore::ensure_path_ignored`.

Rubric 2 item 2 (parameter sprawl): `compact_window::Sources` and the `recommend_report(root, main_root, store, sources)` seam are pinned testability seams; `ledger::Ingest` is the same shape. Nothing else grew a parameter.
Rubric 2 item 6 (unnecessary wrapper elements): not applicable — no component-tree UI framework in this crate (the plugin links neither `ratatui` nor `inquire`).
Rubric 2 item 7 (nested conditionals 3+ deep): the deepest nesting in either file is two levels (`plan_starts`'s match inside a match, `read_usage`'s `if let` chain), each with a documented reason.

Rubric 2 item 8 (unnecessary comments): every comment in both files states a rule, a measurement or an invariant (why the head is scanned before the JSON parse, why cost-state is a floor, why an explicit null is not a value). None restates the code or narrates a change, and the plan ids that do appear (R25, R26, AE31, AE33, KTD11) are each followed by the explanation the convention asks for.
Rubric 2 item 10 (context-dependent vocabulary): the vocabulary is consistent with CONCEPTS.md and CLAUDE.md — store, ledger, row, worktree root, main checkout, peak context, window.

Rubric 2 item 11 (pre-release compatibility scaffolding): the two backward-compatible readers here are deliberate and still needed — `read_usage`'s flat `cache_creation_input_tokens` fallback for older transcripts, and `Row::peak_context_tokens` being `Option` for rows written before the field existed. Both are consumed by shipped data on disk, not superseded within this branch.

Rubric 3 item 2 (missed concurrency): the scans are already sequential by design (the expensive scan runs outside the lock, the commit inside it), and parallelising a directory walk over a session's transcripts would change ordering and the hook's process footprint.
Rubric 3 item 4 (recurring no-op updates): no polling, event or reducer loop in either module.

Rubric 3 item 6 (memory): both stores are bounded — the ledger holds one row per session id (`replace_row` keeps it that way) and the scan reads line by line into a reused buffer rather than slurping a transcript.

Test helpers duplicating core's `testutil`: none. `compact_window/tests.rs` already uses `testutil::{exit_code_to_u8, init_main_repo}`; its remaining helpers (`fixture`, `read_local_settings`, `gitignore_contents`, `ledger_row`, `store_with`, `sources_with_home`, `snapshot`) build shapes `testutil` does not provide.
